title: Before filing an EEOC charge of discrimination: information and documents to gather
use_when: Use when a private-sector, state or local government, union or staffing-agency worker or applicant is preparing an EEOC inquiry, intake interview and charge of employment discrimination; federal employees and applicants follow a different complaint process.
note: Built from EEOC's How to File a Charge, Time Limits, and What You Can Expect pages, the EEOC Public Portal User's Guide Vol 2 (February 27, 2019), and the evidence chapter of the EEOC Compliance Manual (CM-602, issued 02-01-1988). EEOC states a charge generally must be filed within 180 calendar days of the discrimination, extended to 300 days where a state or local agency enforces a law against discrimination on the same basis (for age, only a state law and state agency extend it); the deadline applies to each discrete event, and for harassment it runs from the last incident. It does not assess whether the claim is covered or timely, and does not cover state FEPA procedures, Equal Pay Act lawsuits, or the federal-sector process.

situations.several-events: Did more than one discriminatory event happen (for example a demotion and later a firing)?
situations.harassment: Is the client alleging ongoing harassment?
situations.other-location: Did the client work at a location other than the employer's main address when the discrimination happened?
situations.prior-eeoc: Has the client already filed a charge with the EEOC about this matter?
situations.prior-agency: Has the client already filed a complaint about this matter with another agency (for example a state or local fair employment practices agency)?
situations.attorney: Is an attorney representing the client?

items.label: Your name, address, email and telephone number
items.detail: Listed as required content of a charge letter.

items.label: Name, address, email and telephone number of the employer, employment agency or union
items.detail: The organization the charge is against (the respondent).

items.label: Type of employer
items.detail: The portal first asks for the type: private business or non-profit, union, temp agency or staffing firm, state or local government, or the federal government. Vol 2, Step 2.

items.label: Approximate number of employees at the employer
items.detail: If known. The online inquiry asks the client to pick an approximate range. Vol 2, Step 5.

items.label: Address of the location where you worked, if different from the employer's main address
items.detail: Vol 2, Step 11, Respondent/Employer Information.

items.label: State where the discrimination happened
items.detail: Used with the date to work out the filing deadline. Vol 2, Step 5, Location.

items.label: Short description of each action you believe was discriminatory
items.detail: For example being fired, demoted or harassed.

items.label: Date the discrimination took place
items.detail: The 180/300-day deadline is counted in calendar days from this date, including weekends and holidays.

items.label: Separate date for each discriminatory event
items.detail: The deadline usually applies to each event on its own.

items.label: Date of the last incident of harassment, and a list of the earlier incidents
items.detail: The charge must be filed within 180 or 300 days of the last incident; EEOC looks at all incidents when investigating.

items.label: Why you believe you were treated this way
items.detail: Race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, transgender status and sexual orientation), national origin, age (40 or older), disability, genetic information, or retaliation. Check all that apply.

items.label: Description of the events leading up to the decision
items.detail: CM-602.6(a)(1), background information.

sections.name: Your job and the people involved

items.label: Short summary of your work history with the employer
Your job description and a list of your actual duties
Names and job titles of the employer's people involved in the decision
Names of similar co-workers who were treated the same as you, and those treated differently
Names of witnesses who know about what happened
items.detail: EEOC asks the charging party to identify witnesses and evidence, mostly during the intake interview. CM-602.3 and 602.6(c).

items.label: Documents that support your charge
items.detail: Can be uploaded through the EEOC Public Portal.

items.label: Date and charge number of the earlier EEOC charge
items.detail: Vol 2, Step 11, Previous Filing Information (date required).

items.label: Name of the other agency, the date filed, and what the complaint was about
items.detail: All three are required. Vol 2, Step 11, Previous Filing Information.

items.label: Letter of representation from your attorney
items.detail: Can be uploaded through the EEOC Public Portal.
